verdict.rationale: Omarchy bundles Claude Code and OpenCode as default agent harnesses and notes these are 'particularly helpful when having an AI agent work with you on customization or configuration,' implying some natural-language operability for system config tasks. However, there's no dedicated natural-language command interface for the OS/desktop itself — Omarchy's stated interaction paradigm is keyboard-driven ('Everything in Omarchy happens via the keyboard'), and AI dictation (Voxtype) is speech-to-text, not command execution. Missing for 10: evidence of a native NL command/assistant layer for operating Omarchy's own UI/settings, independent confirmation that agents can actually control the desktop environment, and any first-party API/CLI designed for NL-driven automation.
